1.explanation:
This script:
1. Spins up an Express server on port 8080 that logs every incoming request’s User-Agent header.
2. Launches a headless Chrome instance via chrome-launcher.
3. Runs Lighthouse against the local server URL with mobile emulation (emulatedFormFactor:'mobile'), which sets Nexus 5 dimensions and a mobile UA override.
4. After Lighthouse completes, it prints the userAgent string that Lighthouse embeds in the report (lhr.runtimeSettings.userAgent) and the actual UA headers the server saw.

You will observe the two strings differ, reproducing the mismatch between “Runtime settings → User agent” and the UA seen in network logs.
1.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse in mobile emulation (e.g. emulated Nexus 5) the user‐agent string printed under “Runtime settings” in the resulting report does not match the actual User-Agent header sent in the network requests. In our tests you can see Lighthouse reporting a CrOS/Linux UA in the report, but your webserver logs show a mobile Android UA (or vice versa).
